info.name: AMS Infotainment — by Page
info.description:
The AMS Infotainment frontend's API calls, organised by the PAGE that fires them so you can see, section by section, exactly what data each part of a page is querying.

WHY THIS EXISTS
The UI is right but some sections show the wrong data. Each request below is labelled with the exact on-screen section it feeds and the exact params the Next.js app sends (page_size, slug, ids). Fire a request, look at `data`, and check it matches the section. Where a block uses a HARDWIRED category slug (the landing-page tail, the article sidebar), a wrong slug here is the usual cause of wrong data.

HOW IT MAPS TO THE CODE
Every request names its source: e.g. `src/lib/home-data.ts → getHomeFeed`. The base client is `src/lib/api/client.ts` (apiFetch). All reads are server-side.

ENVELOPES
- List endpoints (get-articles, get-article-by-category-slug, tv-show-episodes):
  { status:'OK', data:[...], page, per_page, total, total_page }
  GOTCHA: get-articles returns `total` as a STRING; get-article-by-category-slug returns it as a NUMBER.
- Single-object (web/episode, web/program, web/featured-program):
  { status:'OK', data:{...} }  — featured-program can return data:null (banner hidden), NOT a 404.
- get-article-by-slug: a RAW object, NO {status,data} envelope.
- Core wp/v2/* (posts, categories, users, comments, pages, episode): plain WordPress REST shapes.

VARIABLES — a few requests need a real id/slug you paste in (article_slug, episode_id, author_id). The quickest source is noted on each. Category-scoped requests already carry real slugs so they send as-is.

Backends: `wp/v2/web/*` split across two WP plugins — AMS3E-API (articles/menu) and our AMS Frontend API (tv-show-episodes, episode, featured-program, hero-embed). `wp/v2/posts|categories|users|comments|pages|episode` are WordPress core. `/api/revalidate` is the Next.js app itself.

A sibling collection, ams-infotainment-api.postman_collection.json, documents the same endpoints grouped by BACKEND instead of by page (and includes endpoints the frontend does not use).

Generated from the code on 2026-07-16.

item.name: 🌐 Global — Header & Footer (every page)
item.description:
The site shell wraps every route (src/app/layout.tsx → SiteHeader / SiteFooter).

ONLY ONE live API call: the category tree, which builds the header's section→topic→{news,reports} menu. Everything else in the shell is HARDCODED in the frontend and hits no API:
- Nav pills, digital-content icon strip, program posters → src/lib/navigation.ts (static registry)
- Footer link columns, legal links, newsletter CTA, socials → src/lib/home-data.ts + src/lib/site.ts (static)

The category tree is also the shared lookup (id → listing URL, and taxonomy depth) that nearly every other page uses to turn a category id into a link. If category chips or breadcrumbs point at the wrong place site-wide, start here.

item.name: Category tree (nav menu + shared id→href lookup)

query.description: parent is needed to rebuild the section→topic tree; link is the real URL path.

request.description:
SECTION: header dropdown menu (SiteHeader), plus the id→href / id→depth maps used across the app.
SOURCE: src/lib/categories.ts → getCategoryTerms / getNavMenu / getCategoryHrefs / getCategoryDepths / resolveCategory.

Returns the 26 terms. The app TRANSPOSES this (WP nests contentType→section→topic; the menu shows section→topic→{news,reports}) and sorts topics by a hand-written order (TOPIC_ORDER) because the taxonomy carries no term_order.

DEBUG: a term's `link` (e.g. …/category/celebrity/news/) is the source of truth for its URL — the app reads the path out of it, not out of the slug. Wrong chip/breadcrumb links usually trace to a term whose `link` changed in WP.

item.name: 🏠 Homepage ( / )
item.description:
Route: src/app/page.tsx. Data: src/lib/home-data.ts → getHomeFeed (one Promise.all of the 8 calls below) + getFeaturedPrograms (static).

SECTION → REQUEST
- ព្រឹត្តិការណ៍ប្រចាំថ្ងៃ (Daily Events), 3 tabs → 'Today' (get-articles) + 'Yesterday' + 'Day before' (core posts date windows)
- របាយការណ៍ថ្មីៗ (Latest Reports) → reports feed
- Lifestyle grid → life-style-news feed
- Video feature banner → featured-program
- Health grid → tv-show-episodes (1-minute-for-health)
- Obsok grid → tv-show-episodes (obsok)
- Hero slider → /hero-embed iframe (HTML, not JSON)

STATIC (no API): PosterBand, PopularPrograms band, nav pills — all from src/lib/navigation.ts.

NOTE ON DRIFT: the by-backend collection still lists the daily grid at page_size=9; the code now sends page_size=5 (below). If a section shows too many/too few items, the page_size here is the truth.

Every grid FALLS BACK to curated mock data on error, so an empty/failed API call shows placeholder content rather than a blank — a section 'showing wrong data' can also mean 'showing the fallback'.

query.description: 6913 = all-news (ព្រឹត្តិការណ៍), the news root. DIRECT assignments only — it does NOT aggregate the subtree.

request.description:
SECTION: Daily Events widget, ថ្ងៃនេះ tab (lead card + 2×2 cluster).
SOURCE: home-data.ts → getHomeFeed → fetchHomeCards(…&category_id=6913).

DELIBERATELY NOT DATE-FILTERED: this is the newest five of the news root, not 'today'. The tab must render a lead + four on every load, and a true today-window returns only what has published so far (1 article mid-morning, 0 before the day's first post). The other two tabs ARE true day windows.

SCOPE GOTCHA: category_id matches DIRECT term assignments — 6913 reaches ~780 of the site's ~10,450 articles, not all of them. Every recent article carries the root tag (so this returns the same 5 as the unscoped feed), but slug=all-news would aggregate the subtree instead (10,283) and is NOT equivalent.

Item: { id, title, categories[{id,name,slug}], category, slug, post_date (relative Khmer), thumbnail, description }.

exec: // Yesterday's calendar day in Asia/Phnom_Penh (UTC+7), mirroring src/lib/wp-core.ts dayStart().
const d = new Date(Date.UTC(pp.getUTCFullYear(), pp.getUTCMonth(), pp.getUTCDate() - off));

query.description: Phnom-Penh midnight starting yesterday (set by pre-request script).
Phnom-Penh midnight starting today (set by pre-request script).
6913 = all-news (ព្រឹត្តិការណ៍), the news root — core's `categories` also matches DIRECT assignments only.
resolves the thumbnail + category terms
trims ~3–4MB of payload; _links must stay for _embed to work

request.description:
SECTION: Daily Events widget, ម្សិលមិញ tab — a TRUE calendar-day window, scoped to the news root.
SOURCE: wp-core.ts → fetchDayCards(1, 6913). Uses WordPress CORE posts, NOT get-articles: get-articles' own date_filter ('1day_ago') OVERLAPS yesterday+today, so the clean per-day bucket has to come from an after/before window.

The 6913 scope is a no-op on recent days (every recent article carries the root tag — verified 5/5 for yesterday), but it enforces the ព្រឹត្តិការណ៍ meaning going forward.

Core returns a different shape (title.rendered, thumbnail behind _embedded['wp:featuredmedia']). The pre-request script fills after/before with Phnom-Penh midnights so this returns the same day the site shows.

const d = new Date(Date.UTC(pp.getUTCFullYear(), pp.getUTCMonth(), pp.getUTCDate() - off));

query.description: the section shows 4 cards
explicit comma-separated category IDs — returns articles in ANY of them (a UNION). Replaces the old slug=reports subtree aggregation.

request.description:
SECTION: របាយការណ៍ថ្មីៗ (Latest Reports).

QUERY-BY-ID (new approach): get-articles with an explicit category_id list, instead of get-article-by-category-slug?slug=reports. `category_id` takes comma-separated IDs and returns the UNION — you pin the exact categories rather than letting the backend aggregate one slug's subtree (which is what was pulling the wrong articles in).

SOURCE: home-data.ts → getHomeFeed (fetchHomeCards). The frontend now sends THIS query — migrated from slug=reports on 2026-07-16.

IDs: 971 = reports root (បទយកការណ៍), 989 = life-style-health-and-beauty-reports, 991 = life-style-life-tips-reports. This union ≈ 171 items vs 173 for the full slug=reports subtree; the top cards match. Item shape is IDENTICAL to the slug endpoint (same 8 fields), so no mapper change was needed.

SECTION: Lifestyle grid.
SOURCE: home-data.ts → getHomeFeed (fetchHomeCards, slug=life-style-news).

query.description: 1-minute-for-health tv_show id
the app fetches the WHOLE show (up to 200/page) then keeps the newest 12

request.description:
SECTION: Health grid (12 cards).
SOURCE: home-data.ts → fetchEpisodeCards('1-minute-for-health', 14570, 12) → episodes.ts fetchShowEpisodes.

WHY page_size=200 not 12: the whole show is fetched so slugs can be de-duplicated across the full list (a page of 12 in isolation would emit hrefs the router 404s on). The 12 shown are the newest after sorting. Item: { id, title, episode_number ('S1:E12'), permalink, post_thumbnail }.

query.description: obsok tv_show id

request.description:
SECTION: Obsok grid (12 cards).
SOURCE: home-data.ts → fetchEpisodeCards('obsok', 14512, 12). Same mechanics as the Health grid.

SECTION: VideoFeatureStrip (wide video banner). Also appears above the footer on program/episode pages.
SOURCE: src/lib/featured-program.ts → getFeaturedProgram.

WHICH program + the banner art are set in WP admin (Settings → Featured Program), not in code. Returns { status:'OK', data:{…} } or data:null (banner hidden — NOT a 404).
data: { id, slug, title, description(HTML), permalink, poster(PORTRAIT), cover(WIDE banner), release_date(Unix, midnight Phnom Penh), schedule, tv_show_id, video:{choice,url,attachment,embed} }.
GOTCHAS: poster≠cover (portrait vs ultra-wide); prefer video.url over the stale video.embed.

item.name: 📄 Article page ( /article/[slug] )
item.description:
Route: src/app/article/[slug]/page.tsx. Data: articles.ts → getArticle + getArticleExtras, comments.ts → getComments.

SECTION → REQUEST
- Main article (title, body, featured image, author, breadcrumb) → get-article-by-slug
- Comment count + thread → comments (read)
- Sidebar 'ប្រធានបទពេញនិយម' / below-body 'ព័ត៌មានសង្ខេប' / 'ព័ត៌មានផ្សេងៗទៀត' / prev-next pager → get-articles page_size=24 (ONE feed, sliced into disjoint windows)
- Below-body 'របាយការណ៍ថ្មីៗ' → reports feed
- Below-body 'អត្ថបទកម្សាន្ត' → entertainment-news feed
- Sidebar 'រសជាតិ' → life-style-travel-news
- Sidebar 'ស្នេហានិងទំនាក់ទំនង' → life-style-love-and-relation-news
- Sidebar 'ភាពយន្ត' → entertainment-movie-and-music-news
- Comment submit → POST comments (REST), fallback POST wp-comments-post.php

STATIC: the program strip below the article is the hardcoded registry (navigation.ts).

DEBUG — this is a prime suspect for 'wrong data in a section': the three sidebar widgets have EDITORIAL headings that are NOT their term names (រសជាតិ='flavour' heads the TRAVEL feed; ភាពយន្ត heads movie-and-music). Each request below names both the heading and the slug it should be pulling — verify the pairing.

query.description: Set the article_slug variable, or grab one from Homepage → Daily Events (data[].slug).

request.description:
SECTION: the whole main column — featured image, title, meta line, body, author box, breadcrumb.
SOURCE: articles.ts → getArticle.

RAW object, NO {status,data} envelope. Fields: { id, title, thumbnail, categories[{id,name}], publish_date ('YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'), last_updated, description, post_content (Gutenberg HTML), author{id,author_name,profile,description}, seo{title,description} }.
NOTE: detail `categories` carry NO slug (only id+name) — the app joins them to the Global category tree by id to build breadcrumb/chip links.

query.description: the article's WP post id (the `id` from Article detail). Set an article_id var or paste it here.
oldest first, how the thread reads

request.description:
SECTION: the comment COUNT in the meta line (and the thread itself).
SOURCE: src/lib/comments.ts → getComments. WordPress core — only APPROVED comments come back, threaded via `parent`.
NOTE: the visible comments list component is currently commented out in the page, but the count is still rendered from this call.

item.name: Recent feed — sidebar 'popular' + summaries + other-news + prev/next

request.description:
SECTION: four blocks are DISJOINT windows of this one 24-item feed —
- sidebar ប្រធានបទពេញនិយម → items 0–4
- ព័ត៌មានសង្ខេប (summaries) → items 5–12
- ព័ត៌មានផ្សេងៗទៀត (other news) → items 13–21
- prev/next pager → items 22, 23
SOURCE: articles.ts → getArticleExtras → recentRefs(24).
The windows are disjoint on purpose so no article appears twice on the page. These blocks are the ones with NO category in their name; the category-named blocks are fetched from their own term (below).

item.name: 🗂️ Category listing ( /category/[...path] )
item.description:
Route: src/app/category/[...path]/page.tsx. Data: categories.ts → resolveCategory (uses the Global category tree) + articles.ts → getCategoryPage.

SECTION → REQUEST
- Main article list (featured card + rows) + pagination → get-article-by-category-slug page_size=10
- Sidebar 'ប្រធានបទពេញនិយម' → THIS category, page_size=3
- Sidebar 'របាយការណ៍' → reports, page_size=3
- Sidebar 'អត្ថបទពេញនិយម' ('most read') → get-articles page_size=3 (no view-count field exists, so it's honest recents)

DRIFT NOTE: the by-backend collection lists page_size=11 for the listing; the code sends page_size=10 (1 featured + 9 rows).

This route serves LISTINGS (/category/celebrity/news); the magazine LANDING pages (/celebrity) are a separate route — see the '🎯 Landing pages' folder.

query.description: term SLUG (e.g. all-news, entertainment-news). Aggregates over the term's descendants.
the URL's /page/N segment maps here
1 featured card + 9 rows; total_page is derived from this

request.description:
SECTION: the main article list and the pagination footer.
SOURCE: articles.ts → getCategoryPage. `total_page` drives Pagination — change page_no to see later pages.

item.name: Sidebar 'ប្រធានបទពេញនិយម' (this category's latest)

request.description:
SECTION: sidebar widget 1 — the ONLY block scoped to the term you're viewing.
SOURCE: getCategoryPage → categoryRefs(category, 3). It used to render global recents on every listing; must now match {{category_slug}}.

SECTION: sidebar widget 2 — បទយកការណ៍.
SOURCE: getCategoryPage → categoryRefs('reports', 3). Named for reports, so it comes from the reports tree (it used to leak news articles).

request.description:
SECTION: sidebar widget 3 — 'most read'.
SOURCE: getCategoryPage → recentRefs(3). There is NO view-count field anywhere in REST, so this is deliberately most-recent site-wide, not a real ranking.

item.name: 🎯 Landing pages — Section & Topic ( /celebrity, /life-style … )
item.description:
Route: src/app/[...path]/page.tsx (the site's ROOT catch-all). Data: categories.ts → resolveLanding + landing-data.ts → getLandingFeed.

These are the ELEVEN magazine landing pages (2 sections + 9 topics), distinct from the /category listings. Section pages: /entertainment-news, /life-style. Topic pages: /celebrity, /movie-and-music, /strange, /culture, /life-style/travel, /life-style/love-and-relation, /life-style/health-and-beauty, /life-style/life-tips, /life-style/architecture.

WHY THIS IS THE #1 SUSPECT FOR WRONG DATA: almost every block on a landing page is HARDWIRED to a specific category slug (see landing-data.ts TAIL/MATIKA/FEATURES) — NOT to the page's own term. Two sections and nine topics all render the same tail. So a block can be 'correct by design' yet look wrong for the page you're on. Each request names the exact block heading + slug the code sends; the subfolders separate the section-only head, the topic-only head, and the tail shared by all eleven.

STATIC: the សម្រាប់លោកអ្នក poster band = getFeaturedPrograms(15) from the registry (no API).

Static WP pages (/contact, /jobs, …) also resolve through this same route — see the '📃 Static pages' folder.

item.description: Every landing page — section AND topic — renders this identical tail from HARDWIRED slugs. If a tail block looks wrong, check the heading↔slug pairing named on each request. Also: the two feature banners and the team list are the same on every page.

item.name: Matika tab 1 — Love (ស្នេហានិងទំនាក់ទំនង)

item.name: 📃 Static pages ( /contact, /jobs, /privacy-policy … )
item.description:
Route: src/app/[...path]/page.tsx (same catch-all as landing pages; resolves here when the path isn't one of the 11 landings). Data: src/lib/pages.ts → getStaticPage.

Seven whitelisted WP pages: advertising, contact, question, jobs, privacy-policy, terms-conditions, cookies. Two requests back the lot: an index (path→id) then the page body.

GOTCHA: the index is keyed on the page's PERMALINK, not its slug — /terms-conditions/ is served by a page whose slug is Khmer, so ?slug=terms-conditions returns [].

query.description: link is the permalink the app keys on

request.description:
SECTION: resolves which WP page id serves a given /path.
SOURCE: pages.ts → getPageIndex. Only the 7 whitelisted paths are actually served (the CMS holds ~55 pages, most of them drafts/ad mockups).

SECTION: the static page's <h1> + body.
SOURCE: pages.ts → getStaticPage. Set page_id from the Page index (e.g. the id whose link ends /contact/). content.rendered is Gutenberg HTML, same shape as an article body.

item.name: 📺 Program overview ( /program/[slug] )
item.description:
Route: src/app/program/[slug]/(overview)/page.tsx. Data: programs.ts → getProgram + articles.ts → categoryRefs ×2 + home-data.ts → getHomeFeed + getFeaturedPrograms (static).

The UNIQUE calls are below. Everything from DailyEventsSection down is the HOMEPAGE'S OWN FURNITURE — the same 8 calls as the '🏠 Homepage' folder (getHomeFeed) plus the static poster carousel. Not repeated here.

Example values use អផ្សុក (obsok): post id 14562, tv_show id 14512. Swap program_post_id / program_show_id for another show (id table in src/lib/programs.ts). REMEMBER: a program's post id and tv_show id are DIFFERENT numbers.

query.description: the program POST id (movie/tv_show), NOT the tv_show id

request.description:
SECTION: ProgramHero + ProgramAbout (title, description, poster, backdrop, year, schedule).
SOURCE: programs.ts → fetchProgramMeta → web/program?id=<postId>.
Goes through our own endpoint (not core wp/v2/movie) because the backdrop lives in Vodi post meta core REST won't expose. GOTCHA: `schedule` is the broadcast slot text, stored in MasVideos' run_time field — it is NOT a duration.

query.description: the tv_show id (≠ program_post_id)

request.description:
SECTION: EpisodeCarousel (newest 18) + SeasonTabs (grouped by season).
SOURCE: programs.ts → getProgram → fetchEpisodeCards(slug, showId, 18) + fetchSeasonCards (one shared, cached fetch).
The upstream orders by POST DATE, not episode order, so the app re-sorts by the episode-number label. If the carousel order looks wrong, that sort (episodes.ts compareEpisodes) is where to look — not this raw response.

SECTION: ProgramNews left column.
SOURCE: program page → categoryRefs('entertainment-news', 3).

SECTION: ProgramNews right column.
SOURCE: program page → categoryRefs('all-news', 3).
+ Below this: the entire Homepage feed (see 🏠 Homepage folder) renders on the program page too.

request.description:

data: { id, title, episode_number, run_time, release_date (Unix, midnight Phnom Penh), tv_show_id, tv_show_title, season_id, season_name, post_thumbnail, video:{choice,url,attachment,embed} }.
GOTCHAS: format release_date in Asia/Phnom_Penh (Vodi prints it a day early); prefer video.url over the stale video.embed.

request.description:

SOURCE: episode.ts → fetchVimeoRunTime. Vimeo's public oEmbed (no auth) is authoritative on length; WordPress's _episode_run_time is wrong on ~half the episodes and is only the fallback. NOT a WordPress call — it hits vimeo.com directly.

item.name: 🎬 All episodes ( /program/[slug]/episodes )
item.description:
Route: src/app/program/[slug]/episodes/page.tsx. Data: episodes.ts → fetchShowEpisodes → groupSeasons. The 'មើលទាំងអស់' link from a season browser lands here.

One endpoint, paginated: the app pulls page_no=1 first, reads total_page, then fetches the rest (page_size=200, capped at 10 pages) and sorts the whole show by episode-number label.

request.description:
SECTION: the full SeasonGrid list (e.g. daily-feed has 617).
SOURCE: episodes.ts → fetchShowEpisodes. Read total_page in the response; increment page_no to fetch subsequent pages (the app fetches them all, up to 10 pages).

item.name: 👥 Author ( /author, /author/[slug] )
item.description:
Routes: src/app/author/page.tsx (index) and src/app/author/[...path]/page.tsx (archive). Data: authors.ts + wp-core.ts.

SECTION → REQUEST
- /author index grid → All authors
- /author/<slug> header (name, bio) → Author by slug
- /author/<slug> main list + pagination → Author's posts (core)
- /author/<slug> sidebar → 3 category feeds (all-news / reports / entertainment-news, each page_size=3)

request.description:
SECTION: the /author index grid.
SOURCE: authors.ts → getAuthors. WordPress only lists accounts with published content, so this is exactly the set of archives worth linking. avatar_urls are the blank Gravatar for every author (real portraits aren't in REST).

SECTION: /author/<slug> title band + bio.
SOURCE: authors.ts → getAuthorBySlug. Returns an array; the app takes [0]. Read the `id` here for the posts request below.

query.description: the author's user id (from Author by slug)
the /page/N URL segment

SECTION: the author's article list + pagination.
SOURCE: wp-core.ts → fetchAuthorPosts. Uses WordPress CORE posts (get-articles can't filter by author). The page count comes from the X-WP-TotalPages RESPONSE HEADER, not the body — check Headers to see how many pages Pagination will show.
